title: Timebox trial tally — Raja
content:
Quick personal tracker for short timebox experiments. Purpose: run a handful of focused trials (1–3 hours each) to check cost/latency tradeoffs for small-response workloads (chat snippets ~ 30–120 tokens). Use this sheet to decide which configs get promoted to the formal bench infra.

Notes / rules of the road:
- Timebox = max 3 hours continuous (measured wall-clock).
- Each row = one run (one config sweep or stable run).
- Keep baseline run every morning (baseline-v1) so diffs are comparable.
- Use shorthand: Q8 = 8-bit quant, Q4 = 4-bit, KVcache=on/off, burst = short burst autoscale enabled.
- Cost is rough (cloud billing est) — record as cents per 1k tokens.
- Status: quick-pass | check-further | noisy | discard.

TABLE (CSV-ish):
Date,RunID,Model,Quant,Batch,SeqLen,TotalTokens,Requests,LatencyP50_ms,LatencyP95_ms,CostPer1kTok_cents,DeltaVsBaseline_pct,KVcache,Notes,Status
2025-11-12,rb-20251112-01,redwood-llama-13b,Q8,1,64,1800,30,54,128,1.8,0,off,initial baseline,quick-pass
2025-11-12,rb-20251112-02,redwood-llama-13b,Q4,1,64,1800,30,47,110,1.2,-8,off,aggressive quant,check-further
2025-11-13,rb-20251113-01,redwood-llama-13b,Q4,4,64,7200,120,59,150,0.95,-47,on,batched + kvcache,quick-pass
2025-11-15,rb-20251115-03,redwood-mistral-7b,Q8,1,128,3600,28,40,95,1.1,-39,off,good latency but cost medium,check-further
2025-12-02,rb-20251202-01,redwood-mistral-7b,Q4,2,128,7200,60,53,138,0.62,-66,on,burst enabled,quick-pass
2026-01-18,rb-20260118-05,redwood-llama-13b,Q8,2,96,5400,45,62,172,1.5, -17,off,noisy,retry-later
2026-02-10,rb-20260210-02,redwood-llama-13b,Q4,1,96,1800,20,49,123,1.0,-46,on,kv warm cache,quick-pass

Quick observations (personal):
- Q4 consistently drops cost but P95 sometimes regresses when batch=1; acceptable for conversational flows if P95 < 140ms.
- KVcache ON + small batching (2–4) gives the best cost/latency blend for repeated short prompts.
- Burst policy reduced tail events during peak test at 2025-12-02. Need to test at different seq lengths (32, 64, 128) to generalize.
- Baseline drift: morning baseline often 3–6% faster than later runs — maybe node allocation coldness or metadata effects. Add a quick warmup step.

To-do (next timebox):
- Run 6 x 30-min sweeps comparing Q8 vs Q4 across seq=32/64/128 with KVcache toggled.
- Add micro-tracing for any run with P95 > 150ms to capture scheduling spikes. Link traces to runID.
- Convert top 2 configs to formal bench job and submit PR with perf/data.

Scratch section (questions / hypotheses):
- H1: For <100-token responses, Q4 + KVcache + batch 2 dominates cost per token.
- H2: Tail latency spikes are correlated with lower GPU core utilization during small-batch, single-request patterns.
- Quick checks: check node mem fragmentation, and compare with compaction-enabled runtime.

Recent quick log: 
- 2026-02-20: reproduced a noisy P95 on llama-13b Q8 (rb-20260220-01) — traced to a stale load-balancer rule. Fixed; re-run scheduled.

Personal reminder: keep runs named rb-YYYYMMDD-XX, record linked PR/trace IDs in the Notes field when available.

End of sheet.
